answer:
RESULT — "At what SES level is the completion-rate advantage for Black students most pronounced?"

CORE FINDING: Black students do NOT exceed White students at any single SES level, but the Black–White completion gap NARROWS MONOTONICALLY as SES rises and is essentially closed (near parity) at HIGH SES. That high-SES convergence is where the Black "advantage" (i.e., the closing of the disadvantage / matching the reference) is most pronounced.

HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, plain language):
"The gap between Black and White BA-completion rates narrows steadily as socioeconomic status rises, so the Black advantage — understood as the point where the Black rate meets the reference rate — is most pronounced at HIGH SES. In the top-SES group (SES > +0.5 SD, the upper third), Black students complete a BA at 3.45% vs White 3.54% (diff −0.10 pp, n_Black=232, n_White=1552), i.e., near parity, and Black students marginally EXCEED Hispanic students at high SES (3.45% vs 3.36%, +0.09 pp, n_Black=232, n_Hispanic=149). At low and mid SES the Black rate is clearly below the White reference (tertiles — Low: 0.44% vs 3.05%, diff −2.61 pp; Mid: 1.87% vs 3.54%, diff −1.67 pp), so there is no SES level at which Black students show a clear, positive completion advantage over White; the effect is best described as convergence to parity at high SES."

TABLE (completion % = % with BA DEGREE COMPLETED=1; pp = Black minus reference, percentage points):

Tertile binning (cutpoints SES ≤ −0.34 / ≤ 0.227 / > 0.227):
  SES    Black%  n   White%  n   Hisp%  n   B−W(pp)  B−H(pp)
  Low     0.44  906   3.05  1245  0.78  774   −2.61   −0.33
  Mid     1.87  802   3.54  1834  1.73  289   −1.67   +0.14
  High    2.22  405   3.81  2258  3.08  260   −1.59   −0.85

SD-based binning (sensitivity; cutpoints −0.5 / +0.5):
  SES          Black%  n   White%  n   Hisp%  n   B−W(pp)  B−H(pp)
  Low(<−0.5)    0.46  651   1.74  805   0.61  655   −1.28   −0.15
  Mid(−0.5..0.5) 1.38 1230   4.03  2980  1.93  519   −2.64   −0.54
  High(>0.5)    3.45  232   3.54  1552  3.36  149   −0.10   +0.09

Overall (all SES): Black 1.33% (n=2113), White 3.54% (n=5337), Hispanic 1.44% (n=1323).

WORKFLOW NOTE: Loaded nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 rows, 0 missing in all columns). Computed completion rate = P(BA DEGREE COMPLETED=1) per race within each SES bin; binned continuous, ~standardized SES two ways — tertiles (equal-n) as primary and ±0.5 SD as sensitivity. Reported Black vs White (primary reference), Black vs Hispanic, and Black vs pooled non-Black per bin, with n and completer counts per cell. Identified the SES level with the smallest (most favorable) Black–reference gap.

LIMITATIONS / CAVEATS:
- No bin yields a clear, positive Black advantage over White; the "advantage" is really convergence to parity at high SES (−0.10 pp, statistically indistinguishable from 0).
- High-SES cells are small (Black n=232, only 8 completers in the SD bin), so the near-parity is within noise.
- Reference-group choice changes the sign: vs Hispanic, Black is at/slightly above parity at high SES (+0.09 pp) and near parity at low SES; vs White, Black is below at every level but closest at high SES.
- Overall completion is very low (~2.7%), making per-cell rates sensitive to a few completers.
